[quote=dhornaper;59789215][B]The Broadcast[/b]

General Fereydun looks straight into the camera with a stern face and delivers his message.

"Citizens, the armed forces has taken control of the administration of Dhornaper.

A transitionary government headed by the army has taken charge today. All Ministers of the dissolved government are to report themselves to the Army Headquarters immediately."

With that, the live broadcast ends. "Report on it constantly, play it over the radio channels as well, and set your web page to have this as the front news article" barks General Fereydun at the director.

With his broadcast aired, he leaves the building and radios Colonel Jamshid. "Have the broadcast aired and reported on constantly over television, civilian radio, and once over the military radio and get the broadcasters to put this at the front of their web pages. Shut off all network connectivity in five minutes, no matter what." "Yes sir" Colonel Jamshid radios back.

With that, General Fereydun gets back into the army truck on his own and makes his way to the Army Headquarters.

[B]On the Presidential Plane[/b]

President Kourosh and Ministers Emam and Jalayer are all tired from their long day in Hydronia. As they all nod off to sleep, a nervous looking flight attendant wakes them up rather irreverently.

"You need to see this." The flight attendant shows them his phone. "I had nothing to do so I checked my phone with the plane WiFi and saw this on the news." The headline of a Hydronian news article reads: "Army Takes Control of Dhornaper".

The President and his Ministers jolt awake and read the article in stunned silence. After a few minutes where no one says anything, the President takes out his phone and connects to the WiFi and attempts to call the Minister of Defence's office. The call fails. Getting desperate, he uses the onboard satellite phone and tries again.

[B]The Ministry of Defence[/b]

The Minister of Defence's satellite phone rings. Minister Dadras, however, is in no position to pick it up. The two soldiers with him in the room have detained him for over an hour and more soldiers surround his ministry's offices. He watches as the phone rings on his desk before it abruptly stops. His habit of working late in the office normally meant he could reliably contacted but today, forces outside his control have made him look unusually absent.

[B]On the Plane Again[/b]

President Kourosh holds his head in his hands as he waits for the call to Dadras to be picked up. After a minute, he cuts it and dials his Director of Intelligence.

[B]In the Director's Apartment[/b]

Director Alavi is sound asleep until he is woken up by the sound of his satellite phone ringing in the other room. Recognising its unique ring tone, he darts straight to it and picks it up.

"Hello President Koroush?"

"What is happening there? Why haven't you called me? The military is launching a coup and you're doing nothing?!"

Director Alavi is shocked. "Sir, a coup? I've been asleep."

"Turn on your television and look for yourself."

Alavi turns on his TV and watches the state broadcaster. On it, he sees the proclamation of General Fereydun on behalf of the army.

"Sir, I'll get the Directorate of Intelligence on it at once."

"Get moving!" is the response shouted back at him.

[B]Back on the Presidential Plane[/b]

President Koroush holds his head in his hands and he thinks over. His Minister of Defence is absent and his Director clueless. With no one else trustworthy he can contact in some position of power over the army, he has to wait as he approaches Dhornaper. According to the pilot, they should be near enough to make radio contact with the air force in approximately 30 minutes. Until then, he hopes that Director Alavi can organise a counter-coup and Minister Dadras can contact him.[/quote]

[B]Alavi's Arrival to the Directorate[/b]

Alavi changes clothes and is out on the street within minutes. He runs as fast as he can to the Directorate of Intelligence offices. When he arrives, he sees three soldiers at the front who block the entrance.

"No entry, go home!"

"I'm Director Alavi, this is my Directorate. Do you want to stand in the way of a Director doing his job? You will be court martialled."

The soldiers exchange looks. "Come with me" one of the soldiers says as he leads Director Alavi inside. The soldier takes Alavi to his sergeant at the reception.

"Sir, the Director is here."

The sergeant looks at Director Alavi. "You are Director Alavi?"

"Yes, I'm here on order of the President."

The sergeant thinks for a moment. "The President's government and position have been dissolved. You're not going anywhere Mr. Alavi." He turns to the soldier "zip tie him to the chair and make sure he goes stays here."

"Yes sir." With that, the soldier grabs Alavi and forces him to his seat before zip tying one of his hands to the chair.

Alavi is stunned and, seeing that he has no escape from the heavily armed soldiers, chooses not to fight his way out. His attempt to save the government is over.

[B]Inside the Army Headquarter's[/b]

The general staff are in disarray. They had no knowledge of the coup and have no idea what is happening. What they do know is that soldiers have occupied the building and no one can go in or out.

"How many units are involved?"
"Is General Fereydun acting on his own or are other generals across the country involved too?"
"Is the air force and navy involved?"

Eventually, a soldier walks in and announces that they must all go to the auditorium. General Fereydun will be there soon.

The general staff stay silent before slowly trickling their way to the auditorium. Not long after, General Fereydun arrives and makes his way to the auditorium stage.

He stands there for a moment, surveying the room before speaking.

"The rest of the army has taken control of the administration and the capital is under control. If you do not support this, you may announce it now and retire from the army without prejudice, no matter your rank."

General Fereydun waits, confident that, as in earlier meetings with his colonels and majors and at the parade field of Major Siamak's company, no one would announce their opposition. After a moment of prolonged silence, General Fereydun continues.

"I will lead the tranistionary government. Order all generals and colonels of the army, all generals of the air force, and all admirals of the navy to present themselves here by tomorrow 12:00 or their reisgnations will be accepted. All generals and colonels present are to remain in the headquarters."

With that, he dismisses the assembled officers who disperse and make a flurry of orders for radio messages and messengers to go out in person to deliver General Fereydun's order. General Fereydun leaves the auditorium and turns towards a staffer passing by. "Prepare a room with ten chairs and a single desk."

"Yes sir."

[B]The President Radios In[/b]

"Sir, we're within radio range of the air force" the pilot announces to the President.

The President walks towards the built-in radio. "Connect me to air base Dashte-e Shar" the president tells a staffer on board. After a moment, the staffer says "you're connected sir."

"This is President Koroush, do you copy?"

After a few moments of silence, a voice answers "President Koroush, I copy."

"There is a military coup ocurring in the capital. I have begun preparations for a counter-coup and I am enroute to your air base. I need to speak to your captain."

On the other end, the voice answers after a pause, "yes sir, please give me a minute to get him."
